Use Tier 2 architectural deepening: add a jointly trained, gated history-summary module to the current ConvRec model. The latest trial improves CDs_and_Vinyl but reduces Electronics HR@10 from 0.420 to 0.355, suggesting that the current representation may favor recent transitions over persistent preferences. This is a hypothesis to test, rather than a confirmed cause of the plateau.

The primary component is model_design: at each sequence position, compute the causal cumulative mean of nonpadding item embeddings and pass it through a learned projection and layer normalization. A learned vector gate, conditioned on both the ConvRec feature and this history summary, will fuse them into one representation before the existing item-scoring layer. Train the entire network jointly with the existing ranking loss; the summary must never produce a separate score or use separately fitted statistics. Apply the same fusion at every supervised training position and at the final inference position, using only the available history window.

The second component is training_evaluation: hold sampling, optimizer, hyperparameters, seeds, and input splits fixed so this experiment isolates the representation change. Select one checkpoint per category using validation HR@10 with 200 users and 99 unique negatives, and report the four-category macro-average alongside category results. Update the predictor writer to reconstruct the added module and load exactly one trained checkpoint per category, with all predictions produced by that network. This adds persistent preference information with linear pooling cost while preserving the single-GPU execution and host-controlled held-out evaluation.
